summary: Calculates pan/tilt rotation values for one or more moving-head style platforms so they point toward target-relative positions while minimizing flips.
key_concepts: Pan Tilt CHOP calculates pan and tilt rotations for moving-head-style platforms aiming at target-relative positions.
The operator minimizes frame-to-frame flipping by choosing the closest equivalent angular rotation.
Multiple rigs can be calculated in one CHOP when channels are ordered consistently per target or fixture.
Input 0 can provide tx, ty, tz relative position channels, or a full Object CHOP transform channel set when rotation is included.
The optional second input can supply pan and tilt reset channels, while Reset Values provide default reset angles in degrees.
Pan and tilt clamp ranges are degree limits and should match the physical fixture's safe travel.

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Discard current rig orientation and use reset values

key_params.name: resetvals
key_params.note: Initial pan/tilt reset values in degrees

key_params.name: resetvals1
key_params.note: Initial pan reset value in degrees

key_params.name: resetvals2
key_params.note: Initial tilt reset value in degrees

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: Input 0 must include tx, ty, tz platform/target-relative channels, or a full standard transform channel set if rotation is included.
The optional reset input must include pan and tilt channels to override reset values per rig.
Use Object CHOP and its DAT table mode when calculating target-to-fixture transforms for multiple rigs.
Clamp ranges are expressed in degrees and should match the physical fixture's safe movement limits.
Pan Tilt CHOP minimizes frame-to-frame flipping, but reset state influences which equivalent orientation is chosen.
Multiple rigs can be calculated per CHOP, so generated channel naming/order must stay consistent with fixture order.
